source: CAMIL GE-V-02 · Page 03 · Family and Introductions (03-Enero-2019)
notes: The page's seven question sentences ('How many people are there in your family?') are
excluded: they are phrases, not lexical items, and the app teaches single entries.
The area is named for what it contains — the 'introductions' half of the page title is
Spelling normalised to standard English where the page hyphenates a closed compound:
GRAND-FATHER -> grandfather, STEP-MOTHER -> stepmother, GOD-FATHER -> godfather. The
page's own IPA confirms these are single words (/ˈɡrænfɑːðər/). Hyphens are kept only
where they are correct: great-grandfather, the in-laws, in-laws.
Units 7 and 8 deliberately hold the pairs that collapse to one Spanish word —
boyfriend/groom and girlfriend/bride are both novio/novia, godfather/best man and
godmother/maid of honor are both padrino/madrina. The learner's difficulty is the
mapping, so the unit is built to be about the distinction rather than to avoid it.
Unit names come from this file, not the model: left to itself it titles every unit after the area, so a learner scrolling the area sees the same heading eight times.

VERY_EASY: this is an A1/A2 course and these are its first pages. Difficulty sets the CEFR level and length of the intro paragraph, not the vocabulary — and it also sets what the unit pays in XP, so a harder unit later is worth more.
